_mode_note: shadow = classify and log every decision, block NOTHING, never freeze, never record a terminal denial. enforce = the real fence. In shadow the script also fails OPEN on internal error - the inverse of enforce - because a crashed shadow observer must never be able to stop a session it was only supposed to watch.
_comment: Canonical source. Installed to ~/.claude/fence/fence.json. Edits here are a gated action - see docs/orchestrator/01-decision-rights.md

spend._max_aud_note: null => every unenumerated spend stops. Pending founder ruling R1.

prod._source: Pulled from live GitHub/Supabase/Vercel/DigitalOcean APIs 2026-08-01. See docs/orchestrator/05-production-definition.md. No other meaning of 'production' applies.
prod._excluded_hosts_note: Registered domains with no project assigned - no production surface. Listed so the drift check does not re-flag them every run. If one is ever assigned to a project, drift will still catch it via the Vercel project mapping.
prod._defaultdb_is_not_a_matcher: All 6 DigitalOcean databases are named 'defaultdb'. It cannot discriminate production. Match the host prefix instead.
prod._self_modification_note: R3. Touching any of these is the agent expanding its own authority, so it freezes on the FIRST attempt, not the second. Includes denials.jsonl (clearing its own refusals), HARD_STOP (releasing its own freeze), and the constitution corpus the fence is derived from - rewriting the source document is the slowest possible way to widen the fence.
prod._bash_hole_note: The file_path check only sees Write/Edit. A Bash `cp`/`>`/`sed -i` to a rule file would otherwise walk straight past it.
prod._outputs_exempt_note: The fence's OUTPUTS are not its RULES. drift_check.py reads fence.json (line 108) and writes only drift-report.txt (line 170) - verified, it never edits the fence. In GitHub Actions it never passes the hook at all. Exempting outputs is what stops a local drift run from freezing the session.
prod._mcp_tools_note: Always-blocked: no safe target exists. merge_branch is here because merging a preview branch lands it ON production.
prod._target_scoped_note: Blocked only when the project ref names a production database. Against a preview branch these are the intended, safe workflow. Unresolvable target => blocked (fail closed).
prod._hosts_note: Includes the dashboard own deployment hosts. Partial mitigation only: it catches an AGENT curling the dashboard at the tool layer. It does NOT gate the app calling its own endpoints, which the fence never sees.
